disagreements.resolution: Closed. WBD's 8-K of 2026-10-06 (Item 2.01) says Skydance Corporation (f/k/a Paramount Skydance) completed the merger on October 6, 2026 at $31.01666668 cash per WBD share; Nasdaq trading halted that day (Item 3.01), Form 25-NSE filed 2026-10-06 and 15-12G on 2026-10-16. A federal judge approved the 12-state settlement on 2026-09-30 (AP). Agents 1, 3 and 5 carry a stale fact: the outside date, the $7B fee and the Kalshi odds are moot. The event now has probability 1. Its effect on Netflix is still uncertain: one owner for HBO Max, Paramount+ and two studios bidding for content and sports, and licensed titles at risk; offset because there is one fewer bidder. I trim the FY28-30 margin by 0.2/0.3/0.3pt (-$0.4 a share) and keep the severe version in the bear case. I did not take agent_4's 1pt UCAN FY27 growth cut, because the '~200M-subscriber merged service' rests on a PPC Land newsletter and AP says only that both services sit 'under the same roof'.

model.reasoning: Primary method (software_internet playbook, streaming): driver DCF on a regional build (paid memberships x ARM, proxied by regional revenue because Netflix stopped reporting members in 2025, with ads inside each region). FY26 is calibrated to the Q3 letter's $51.1B; FY27 +10.2% follows the CFO's 'sustain double-digit revenue growth', then fades to a steady state before a 3% Gordon terminal. The content cash vs amortisation gap sits in capex. Leg weights: DCF 0.2 from the tested forward-P/E band (17.1x FY27); the remaining 0.8 is on 18x NTM GAAP P/E (Liu, Nissim & Thomas 2002: forward P/E is the most accurate single multiple; the P/E vs EV/EBITDA split is judgment, untested). Cross-checks: single-basis 6-peer NTM P/E median 20.4x (set ~12% below); trailing EV/EBITDA core median ~13.9x (DIS/TKO/META/AMZN); engine NTM EBITDA at 14x gives $69.93. Labelled estimates from non-filing evidence: (1) the Paramount-WBD margin trim 0.2-0.3pt (confidence low; variant $71.81, -$0.9, with agent_1's +0.5pt content and -0.5pt growth); (2) FY27 growth from the CFO's wording (medium; variant street +11.5% = +$1.0); (3) peer multiples on Zacks consensus (medium); (4) beta from weekly regressions on Yahoo prices (medium; variant 4.2% ERP = +$0.4). Judgment calls over 5% of fair value: the horizon P/E (19x = $76.1, 16x = $66.1). Round-2 changes vs the round-1 supervisor: Paramount-WBD now closed (FY28-30 margin -0.2/-0.3/-0.3pt) and M&A probability 0.25 -> 0.2. Every other input was re-verified at source this pass.

After revision all five forecasters sit at 18x NTM P/E and fair values of $72.4-74.3; I re-derived the multiple and peer median (20.4x on one basis after the citation gate) myself rather than relying on that convergence. The one new fact I settled is that Paramount-WBD closed on 2026-10-06 (WBD 8-K), which three agents still treated as pending. Its modest margin effect gives a reconciled fair value of $72.74 (bear $49.25 / bull $91.65), within 1% of the mean. key_drivers_text_before: Horizon NTM P/E: 18x on ~$4.15 model EPS (64.89/3.56 = 18.2x today; single-basis 6-peer median 20.4x). Each turn is ~$3.3 a share on fair value.

Engagement vs YouTube: Netflix US TV share 7.9% in June 2026 vs 8.3% in June 2025 (Nielsen Gauge via MediaPost 2026-08-18; Nielsen's June 2025 release) and YouTube at a record 14.2% in July 2026 (Nielsen). The CFO said 'we want to grow view hours faster. We're not satisfied.' The January 2027 FY27 guide and annual engagement report are the tests.
Advertising: 2026 cut to ~$2.7B from ~$3B (Q3 letter); 15 new ad-tier countries in 2027, nine EMEA plus Colombia, Peru and New Zealand from March.
Margin path: FY26 31.5% (incl. the ~120bp Q4 headcount charge) to 33% FY27 and 35.7% FY30, against sports and content inflation and a closed Skydance-WBD rival.
Capital return: Q3 bought 63.9M shares for $4.8B; $22.3B authorisation; FCF ~$12.0B in 2026 returned, shrinking shares ~3% a year.
